title: Common intrinsic cohomology bounds from the retained uniform local integral models
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, T a Noetherian scheme, and K an object of the actual completed integral-coefficient derived category. Uniform bounded constructible reduction local models together with compatible bounded-below etale origins imply PbcUniformReductionProfile T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) K. This is only the cohomological consequence of the local-model hypotheses; it asserts neither completeness nor closure under triangles.

source.place: ## Proof: implicit triangulation needed for the constructible restriction; agent supplement. Stacks Tag 09C3, proetale.tex, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, supplies contextual local models, not this tower-category closure theorem.

proof.text: Choose the common term window [a,b], finite stratification and covering sieves of the given local models. Refine each covering sieve to a scheme pro-etale covering family. Derived scalar extension preserves b. Exact pullback commutes with homology. Its underlying additive inverse image is identified by the canonical adjunction unit; detection by the covers of all strata makes each global cohomology sheaf above b zero.

Transport the local models to the canonical reduction tower using the supplied level isomorphisms. Naturality of the scalar-restriction/pullback comparison and the supplied semilinear transition equations prove every transported normalization square. The upper bound b makes all cohomology modules above the cutoff zero, so higher Tor vanishes there. Apply the existing levelwise truncation existence and constructibility theorem at cutoff b. Its lower truncation vanishes below a-1; the canonical truncation counit is an isomorphism on cohomology in that range. Thus the original canonical tower is bounded below by a-1, independently of the level.

Encode constant-ring module sheaves as fixed-coefficient module sheaves. Exact pullback and scalar-restriction comparisons identify the homology of each pulled-back level with the given local finite-lisse homology. Compose its finite-constant covering family with the chosen cover of the stratum. This proves finite local constancy on every stratum, hence intrinsic constructibility. Finally transport through the supplied level isomorphisms and the exact constant-coefficient restriction and its homology comparison. The bounds [a-1,b] and constructibility give the profile. Empty strata and level zero require no exception. The retained etale origins are unnecessary for this forward implication.

proof_origin.place: Uniform triangulation supplement, step 2; shorter route using the existing levelwise truncation proposition at the common upper bound and direct finite-cover descent.
